summary: What one block does, and why the two additions matter more than they look.

steps.say: One block, one job: let every token look at every other token, then think about what it saw.
Attention is the looking. Each token builds a weighted view of the whole sequence.
Feed forward is the thinking. It runs per token, no mixing, and it is where most of the parameters live.
Stack the two and you have the block.
Now the parts that look like plumbing. These two arrows skip past the layers entirely.

They are the reason depth works at all. Each sub-layer only has to learn a correction to what it received, and the gradient has a path back to the input that never passes through a weight matrix. Remove them and a 96-layer model does not train.
steps.aside: The residual is not plumbing. It is the load-bearing wall.
